title: Hwangnam-daechong Roman Glassware — Glass Ewer and Cups from the South Mound of Tomb No. 98, Gyeongju (National Treasure No. 193)
language_note: Official Korean Heritage Service record is in Korean (경주 98호 남분 유리병 및 잔); English summary from Wikipedia/Met Museum catalogue (Lee & Leidy, Silla: Korea's Golden Kingdom, 2013) used here. No direct textual original — this is an artefact/find record, included for Pillar 4 (multimodal artefact intelligence) rather than text-pair retrieval.
date: late 4th century CE (manufacture, likely Roman Syria); deposited in tomb c. 450 CE
findspot: Hwangnam-daechong tomb (South Mound, Tomb No. 98), Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province, South Korea; excavated 1975
original_text_excerpt: 경주 98호 남분 유리병 및 잔 (慶州 九十八號 南墳 琉璃甁 및 盞) — Glass Ewer and Cups from the South Mound of Tomb No. 98, Gyeongju. Designated National Treasure No. 193, 7 December 1978.
original_text_note: Korean-language official designation and record held by the Korean Heritage Service (citation_original); full descriptive text should be pulled from that record during ingestion.
reference_translation: Set of one ewer (25 x 9.5 cm) and three cups, identified as Late Roman glass, determined on chemical/stylistic grounds to be of Syrian workshop origin (one of four known Roman glass-producing centers: Rome, Alexandria, Cologne, Syria). Imported into the Silla kingdom via Silk Road exchange and deposited as royal grave goods.
translation_source: Summarized from Lee, Soyoung & Leidy, Denise Patry, Silla: Korea's Golden Kingdom (Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2013), pp. 115-131, as reproduced on Wikipedia.
notes: One of the clearest physical-evidence anchors for direct Rome-East Asia material contact via the Silk Road, independent of the textual Weilue/Hou Hanshu sources (eastasia-01, -02). Good candidate for a graph edge linking 'Roman Syria glass workshops' to 'Silla royal tombs' in the Pillar 2 knowledge graph.

findspot_places.name: Gyeongju
findspot_places.note: Confirmed 2026-08-13 against the GeoNames country dump named below; the snapshot date is recorded in data/gazetteer.json under sources.geonames. KR.zip. 1841603 'Gyeongju' 35.843/129.212, feature code P.PPL (populated place), North Gyeongsang — 0.6 km from the Daereungwon tumulus park that holds Hwangnam-daechong. **The coordinate denotes the modern city, not the tomb**: GeoNames has no entry for Tomb No. 98 or its south mound, and none was invented. Refused: 1833276 'Gyeongju' 35.833/129.250, which carries the same name and is A.ADM2 — the municipality, whose representative point sits 3.6 km east of the tumuli and which is a claim about an administrative area rather than about the settlement the record names. Also present and irrelevant: 44 hotels, schools, toll gates and country clubs whose names begin 'Gyeongju'.
